rows: First-level admin region (state / region) of the nearest place; NULL if out of range

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
Return the **first-level administrative region** -- state, province, or region -- of the nearest known place to a latitude/longitude, computed **offline** from the bundled GeoNames index.

## When to use
Use it to roll coordinate data up to a state/province for regional reporting, territory assignment, or joins to administrative reference data.

## Inputs / outputs
- `lat` `DOUBLE` in `[-90, 90]`, `lon` `DOUBLE` in `[-180, 180]`.
- Returns the admin1 name as `VARCHAR`, or `NULL`.

## Behavior & edge cases
- Names follow GeoNames conventions (e.g. `New York`, `Tokyo`, `Bavaria`) and can vary in spelling/transliteration between snapshots.
- `NULL` or out-of-range coordinates return `NULL` (never an error).
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# admin1

First-level administrative region (state / province / region) of the nearest place to `(lat, lon)`, computed offline.

## Usage

```sql
SELECT geocode.main.admin1(40.7128, -74.0060);  -- 'New York'
```

## Notes

GeoNames admin1 label. Returns `NULL` for `NULL`/out-of-range inputs; spelling can drift between bundled snapshots.

rows: Second-level admin region (county/district) of the nearest place; NULL if out of range

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
Return the **second-level administrative region** -- county, district, or borough -- of the nearest known place to a latitude/longitude, computed **offline** from the bundled GeoNames index.

## When to use
Use it for finer-grained geographic rollups than `admin1` (state): county- or district-level reporting, routing, or joins.

## Inputs / outputs
- `lat` `DOUBLE` in `[-90, 90]`, `lon` `DOUBLE` in `[-180, 180]`.
- Returns the admin2 name as `VARCHAR`, or `NULL`.

## Behavior & edge cases
- admin2 is **frequently empty** in GeoNames for many countries, so `NULL` results are common and expected -- not an error.
- `NULL` or out-of-range coordinates also return `NULL`.

# admin2

Second-level administrative region (county / district) of the nearest place to `(lat, lon)`, computed offline.

## Usage

```sql
SELECT geocode.main.admin2(34.0522, -118.2437);  -- 'Los Angeles County'
```

## Notes

Often `NULL` -- admin2 coverage in GeoNames is sparse outside a few countries. Also `NULL` for `NULL`/out-of-range inputs.

rows: ISO-3166 alpha-2 country code of the nearest place; NULL if out of range

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
Return the **ISO-3166 alpha-2** country code (e.g. `US`, `FR`, `JP`) of the nearest known place to a latitude/longitude, computed **offline** from the bundled GeoNames cities index.

## When to use
Use it to attribute coordinate data to a country for grouping, filtering, compliance, or joining to country reference tables -- without any geocoding API.

## Inputs / outputs
- `lat` `DOUBLE` in `[-90, 90]`, `lon` `DOUBLE` in `[-180, 180]`.
- Returns a two-letter `VARCHAR` country code, or `NULL`.

## Behavior & edge cases
- Resolved from the *nearest land place*, so an offshore point yields the code of the closest coastal country.
- `NULL` or out-of-range coordinates return `NULL` (never an error).

# country_code

ISO-3166 alpha-2 country code of the nearest place to `(lat, lon)`, computed offline.

## Usage

```sql

```

## Notes

Two-letter uppercase code. Returns `NULL` for `NULL`/out-of-range inputs; offshore points map to the nearest coastal country.

rows: Great-circle (haversine) distance in km between two points; NULL if out of range

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
Compute the **great-circle (haversine) distance in kilometers** between two `(lat, lon)` points on a spherical Earth. Pure arithmetic -- no index, no lookup, no network.

## When to use
Use it for proximity filtering ('within N km of'), nearest-of ranking, trip length, or any straight-line distance between coordinate pairs in SQL.

## Inputs / outputs
- Four `DOUBLE` arguments: `lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2`, each in the usual lat `[-90, 90]` / lon `[-180, 180]` ranges.
- Returns the distance as a `DOUBLE` in kilometers, or `NULL`.

## Behavior & edge cases
- Uses a mean Earth radius (~6371 km); it is a sphere approximation, not a geodesic on the WGS-84 ellipsoid, so expect sub-percent error.
- If **any** of the four coordinates is `NULL` or out of range the result is `NULL` (never an error).
- Distance is symmetric and zero for identical points.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# distance_km

Great-circle (haversine) distance in kilometers between two points.

## Usage

```sql
SELECT geocode.main.distance_km(40.7128, -74.0060, 51.5074, -0.1278);  -- ~5570
```

## Notes

Spherical approximation (~6371 km radius), sub-percent error vs. WGS-84. Returns `NULL` if any coordinate is `NULL`/out of range.

rows: Name of the nearest known city to (lat, lon); NULL if out of range

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
Return the name of the nearest known populated place (city/town) to a given latitude/longitude, **entirely offline** using a GeoNames cities KD-tree.

## When to use
Reach for this when you have raw coordinate columns (GPS pings, device telemetry, store/asset locations) and want a human-readable place label to group, filter, or display by.

## Inputs / outputs
- `lat` `DOUBLE` in `[-90, 90]`, `lon` `DOUBLE` in `[-180, 180]`.
- Returns a `VARCHAR` city name, or `NULL`.

## Behavior & edge cases
- This is a *nearest-land-place* lookup: the index has no notion of water, so a point in the ocean resolves to the closest coastal city.
- A `NULL` coordinate or one out of range yields `NULL` (never an error).
- City labels track the bundled GeoNames snapshot and can drift slightly between releases.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# nearest_city

Name of the nearest known city to `(lat, lon)`, computed offline from a GeoNames cities KD-tree.

## Usage

```sql
SELECT geocode.main.nearest_city(40.7128, -74.0060);  -- 'New York City'
```

## Notes

Returns `NULL` for `NULL` or out-of-range inputs. Ocean points resolve to the nearest land city; labels follow the bundled GeoNames snapshot.

rows: Nearest place as STRUCT(city, admin1, admin2, country_code, place_lat, place_lon); NULL if out of range

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
Resolve a latitude/longitude to the **full nearest-place record** in a single call, returning a `STRUCT(city, admin1, admin2, country_code, place_lat, place_lon)` computed **entirely offline**.

## When to use
Prefer this over the single-field helpers (`nearest_city`, `country_code`, `admin1`, `admin2`) when you need several attributes at once -- it does the KD-tree lookup once and lets you pluck fields with dot access.

## Inputs / outputs
- `lat` `DOUBLE` in `[-90, 90]`, `lon` `DOUBLE` in `[-180, 180]`.
- Returns a `STRUCT` with `city`, `admin1`, `admin2` (`VARCHAR`), `country_code` (`VARCHAR`), and `place_lat`/`place_lon` (`DOUBLE`, the coordinates of the matched GeoNames place).

## Behavior & edge cases
- For a `NULL` or out-of-range coordinate the **entire struct is `NULL`**.
- Individual fields may be `NULL` (notably `admin2`) even for a valid match.
- Access fields with `reverse_geocode(lat, lon).city`, etc.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# reverse_geocode

Full nearest-place record for `(lat, lon)` as a `STRUCT`, computed offline.

## Columns (struct fields)

| field | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| `city` | VARCHAR | Nearest city / place name. |
| `admin1` | VARCHAR | First-level admin region (state / region). |
| `admin2` | VARCHAR | Second-level admin region (county / district). |
| `country_code` | VARCHAR | ISO-3166 alpha-2 country code. |
| `place_lat` | DOUBLE | Latitude of the matched place. |
| `place_lon` | DOUBLE | Longitude of the matched place. |

## Usage

```sql
SELECT geocode.main.reverse_geocode(40.7128, -74.0060);        -- STRUCT(...)
SELECT geocode.main.reverse_geocode(35.6762, 139.6503).city;   -- 'Tokyo'
```

## Notes

Whole struct is `NULL` for `NULL`/out-of-range inputs; `admin2` is often `NULL`.

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
Return the **IANA timezone name** (e.g. `America/New_York`, `Europe/Paris`, `Asia/Tokyo`) for a latitude/longitude, computed **offline** from bundled IANA timezone polygons (`timezonefinder`).

## When to use
Use it to localize timestamps, derive local time, or bucket coordinate data by timezone -- the returned string drops straight into DuckDB's `timezone(name, ts)` / `AT TIME ZONE`.

## Inputs / outputs
- `lat` `DOUBLE` in `[-90, 90]`, `lon` `DOUBLE` in `[-180, 180]`.
- Returns the IANA tz name as `VARCHAR`, or `NULL`.

## Behavior & edge cases
- Uses true timezone *polygons*, not a nearest-place lookup, so it is exact at borders on land.
- Points outside every tz polygon return `NULL`; some uninhabited ocean cells resolve to a valid `Etc/GMT±N` name instead.
- `NULL` or out-of-range coordinates return `NULL` (never an error).
rows.vgi.doc_md:
# timezone

IANA timezone name for `(lat, lon)`, computed offline from timezone polygons.

## Usage

```sql
SELECT geocode.main.timezone(40.7128, -74.0060);  -- 'America/New_York'
```

## Notes

Polygon-accurate. Returns `NULL` outside all tz polygons and for `NULL`/out-of-range inputs; some ocean cells map to `Etc/GMT±N`.
